name: PhD in Biomedical Informatics
detailsNote: Official information available. The DBMI page gives 'Dec. 1, 2027' for the 2027-28 cohort, which does not match Fall 2027 entry as normally dated; it is published as written and not confirmed. The GRE is not mentioned.
summary: PhD in biomedical informatics from Columbia's Department of Biomedical Informatics. Students rotate through two research labs in their first year before choosing an advisor.

publishedDeadlines.label: Published application deadline (2027-28 cohort)
publishedDeadlines.note: Page says "the deadline for the 2027-28 cohort is currently scheduled to be Dec. 1, 2027." The year looks inconsistent with Fall 2027 entry; not treated as confirmed. Confirm with DBMI.

timeline.interviews: PhD finalists selected for an interview are notified through the admissions portal by late December.

english.note: Scores must be under two years old. Exemptions for a degree from an institution in a country where English is the sole official language, and case-by-case waivers where the language of instruction was English.

applicationFee.note: Fee for the 2027 online application. Waivers are for financial need or hardship, research pathways programs, outside fellowship organizations and US military service; the page does not limit them by citizenship, but confirm eligibility. DBMI says its office cannot provide TOEFL waivers.

requirements.note: Applications are accepted only electronically. Fellowships from the National Library of Medicine are limited to US citizens and permanent residents.

funding.note: GSAS guarantees funding for all Ph.D. students under certain conditions. Funding covers tuition, health insurance fees, University fees and a stipend; the amount is set each summer and given in the offer letter.

international.note: The page asks international applicants to meet the GSAS English requirement; it states no other limit.

sources.label: Columbia GSAS: Information for international applicants
